observation_summary: The compiler incorrectly inferred the type of a 'prototype' property as a string, leading to type mismatch warnings when assigning other types (like functions) to it. The fix involves adding a check to verify if the object being assigned to is a constructor or interface before deciding whether to treat the prototype property as declared.
reasoning_summary: The fix introduces a conditional check (if statement) to validate the type of the class associated with the 'prototype' property. By checking if the class type is a constructor or interface, the compiler can correctly determine whether to skip the inference logic. This is a classic 'Checking' defect where a missing guard condition caused incorrect behavior.
evidence_used: The fix adds an 'if' block in TypedScopeCreator to check if the classType is a constructor or interface.
The bug report states that the compiler incorrectly inferred the type of a prototype property.
The fix uses 'if (classType != null && (classType.isConstructor() || classType.isInterface()))' to guard the return statement.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the logic was changed, the core of the fix is the addition of a guard condition (a check) to prevent incorrect inference, which is the definition of a Checking defect.
